title: Mitosis
short: In prophase chromosomes condense; in metaphase they line up in the middle; in anaphase sister chromatids pull apart; in telophase two nuclei form. Cytokinesis splits the cell into two identical cells.
trouble: Students think the chromosome number halves in mitosis, or that homologous pairs separate. Sister chromatids separate, so each new cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

blocks.html: At the end of G2 a cell has two copies of every chromosome, joined as sister chromatids (The Cell Cycle). Mitosis is the careful dance that gives one copy of each to each new cell.

In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle forms; in metaphase they line up in the middle; in anaphase sister chromatids pull apart to opposite ends; in telophase two nuclei form. Cytokinesis splits the cell into two identical cells.

blocks.name: bi-mitosis
blocks.cap: Step through mitosis with $2n = 4$. Watch the count: four chromosomes at the start, four in each new cell at the end.

head: Stage
What happens
How to spot it
rows: Chromosomes coil up; the nuclear envelope breaks down; spindle fibers form
Thick, visible X-shaped chromosomes scattered in the cell
Chromosomes line up across the middle, each attached to spindle fibers from both poles
A neat line across the center
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
Nuclear envelopes form around each group; chromosomes loosen
The cytoplasm divides (a furrow in animal cells, a cell plate in plant cells)

blocks.html: The key moment is anaphase. In metaphase, each chromosome is attached to spindle fibers from both poles. When the sister chromatids separate, one goes each way. Since every chromosome is lined up and split the same way, each pole gets exactly one copy of every chromosome. The two new cells have the same number of chromosomes as the parent, and the same DNA. That is what growth and repair need: new skin cells that are the same as the old ones.

blocks.title: Count through mitosis
blocks.q: A cell with $2n = 8$ divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes does it have in metaphase, in anaphase (whole cell), and in each new cell?
steps: Anaphase: the 16 chromatids separate and each now counts as a chromosome, so the cell briefly holds 16.
Each new cell gets half of those: 8 chromosomes, the same as the parent.

blocks.html: Thinking the chromosome number halves in mitosis, or that homologous pairs separate. In mitosis the sister chromatids separate; homologs never pair up at all. So each new cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent: 46 in, 46 in each of the two cells out. Halving belongs to Meiosis.
